title: The Longest Strictly Rising Run in a Range, With Changes

concept.title: Like the run of ones, but two runs join at the seam only if the last value of the left part is smaller than the first value of the right part
body: A row of numbers changes one cell at a time. A question asks for the length of the **longest strictly rising run** (consecutive cells with `a[i] < a[i + 1] < ...`) inside a range. For `3 1 2 4 4 5` the longest rising run in the whole row is 3 (the cells `1 2 4`), and inside the cells 4 to 6 it is 2 (`4 5`). Scanning costs O(n) per question.

The node is like the one for the run of ones, with two more values. For its block it stores `len`, `pref` (the length of the rising run at the **left end**), `suf` (the rising run at the **right end**), `best`, and also the first and last values `first` and `last` of the block. Merging `A` and `B`: the runs may join across the seam only if `A.last < B.first`. If they join, then `pref` is `A.len + B.pref` when the whole of `A` is rising (`A.pref == A.len`), else `A.pref`; `suf` is `B.len + A.suf` when the whole of `B` is rising, else `B.suf`; and `best` also considers `A.suf + B.pref`. If they do not join, `pref = A.pref`, `suf = B.suf` and `best = max(A.best, B.best)`.

body.code:
def merge(A, B):                 # (len, pref, suf, best, first, last); an empty node has len 0
    if A[0] == 0: return B
    if B[0] == 0: return A
    join = A[5] < B[4]
    pref = A[0] + B[1] if join and A[1] == A[0] else A[1]
    suf = B[0] + A[2] if join and B[2] == B[0] else B[2]
    best = max(A[3], B[3], A[2] + B[1] if join else 0)
    return (A[0] + B[0], pref, suf, best, A[4], B[5])

body: The empty node must be handled separately, because it has no first and last value. The question joins the left and right accumulators in order. Each operation is O(log n) merges. The same pattern solves "longest non-decreasing run", "longest alternating run" and other properties of neighbouring cells.

statement: A row of `n` numbers is given. Process `q` operations: type 1 `x y` sets the number at the position `x` to `y`; type 2 `x y` asks for the length of the longest block of consecutive cells inside the positions `x` to `y` in which every number is strictly larger than the previous one. Print the answers to the questions on one line, in order.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of cells and the number of operations.
The second line has `n` numbers: the cells.

Each of the next `q` lines has three numbers `t`, `x` and `y`. If `t = 1`, set the cell number `x` to the value `y`. If `t = 2`, print the length of the longest block of consecutive cells inside the cells `x` to `y` whose values are strictly increasing.
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 2, separated by spaces.
constraints: Cells are numbered from 1; for a question 1 <= x <= y <= n.

examples.note: The cells 1 2 4 rise for 3; the cells 4 4 5 give a run of 2: 3 2.

hints: Store (len, prefix run, suffix run, best run, first value, last value).
Two runs join at the seam when the last value on the left is less than the first value on the right.
Handle the empty node separately in the merge.

explanation: Each node stores the block length, the rising run at its left end, at its right end, the best run, and the first and last values; two nodes join their runs at the seam only when the last value on the left is smaller than the first value on the right.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

def merge(A, B):
    if A[0] == 0:
        return B
    if B[0] == 0:
        return A
    join = A[5] < B[4]
    pref = A[0] + B[1] if join and A[1] == A[0] else A[1]
    suf = B[0] + A[2] if join and B[2] == B[0] else B[2]
    best = max(A[3], B[3], A[2] + B[1] if join else 0)
    return (A[0] + B[0], pref, suf, best, A[4], B[5])

n, q = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
ops = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

size = 1
while size < n:
    size *= 2
empty = (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
tree = [empty] * (2 * size)
for i in range(n):
    tree[size + i] = (1, 1, 1, 1, a[i], a[i])
for v in range(size - 1, 0, -1):
    tree[v] = merge(tree[2 * v], tree[2 * v + 1])
out = []
for kind, x, y in ops:
    if kind == 1:
        v = size + x - 1
        tree[v] = (1, 1, 1, 1, y, y)
        v //= 2
        while v:
            tree[v] = merge(tree[2 * v], tree[2 * v + 1])
            v //= 2
    else:
        lo = size + x - 1
        hi = size + y
        left = empty
        right = empty
        while lo < hi:
            if lo & 1:
                left = merge(left, tree[lo])
                lo += 1
            if hi & 1:
                hi -= 1
                right = merge(tree[hi], right)
            lo //= 2
            hi //= 2
        out.append(merge(left, right)[3])
print(*out)
